title: Beyond auxin responses: a miR160-ARF4 module regulates the biogenesis of medicinal saponins
content: Among multiple strategies that plants must adopt to ensure survival fitness, one strategy involves the production of specialized compounds called secondary metabolites. These compounds may not directly regulate growth; however, they play a major role in defense responses and stress adaptation (Jeyasri et al. 2023). Plants produce more than 200,000 secondary metabolites, many of which are used to produce medicines to treat malaria, heart diseases, and cancer (Yonekura-Sakakibara and Saito 2009; Khanam et al. 2025). Yet in many medicinal plants, biosynthesis of these therapeutic compounds can vary based on the developmental stage and environmental conditions (Li et al. 2020). This makes it very difficult to predict and standardize the yield and composition of secondary metabolites for manufacturing pharmaceuticals. Thus, for reliably producing such highly valuable medicinal metabolites, understanding the underlying molecular mechanisms is essential.
